solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One accusing troublemaker, a revolutionary disrupting monarch

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil

indicators.note: to disrupt something is to break into it, so the revolutionary goes inside the monarch

parts.note: ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A mischief-maker and a rebel are accused of plotting against the king.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the article and the revolutionary break into the monarch, not the revolutionary alone. Che Guevara is the setters' stock revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach is to charge a public official formally, so an impeacher is someone bringing an accusation.

clue.text: Instruction to stop — it's extremely hot inside

indicators.note: the word for heat is placed within the word for extremely

parts.note: H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A warning to halt because the place has become unbearably hot within.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside TOO to give TOHO, a call used to make a gun dog stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Toho is a hunter's command telling a dog to halt, so it is literally an order to stop.

clue.text: Sailor has 'idden stock — smuggled thus?

indicators.note: the apostrophe drops the opening aitch Cockney-style, telling you to drop that letter from the next word too

parts.note: a hoard is a stored stock

explanation.surface: A seaman keeps a secret stash, and the question is whether it was brought in illicitly on the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the H of HOARD, as the clue drops it from hidden, and add AB. Goods smuggled by a sailor would be carried aboard, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Contraband slipped onto a vessel is taken on board, so smuggling of that kind is done aboard ship.

clue.text: In windows see pets eating seed

definitions.note: casements are the hinged frames found in windows

indicators.note: pets eating something take it inside them

explanation.surface: Looking through the window, you watch the animals pecking at birdseed.
explanation.walkthrough: Seed tempts you towards birdseed or a plant's seed, but here it is the biological sense. 'In windows' is read loosely: casements are what windows have in them.
explanation.definitionFit: A casement is a window sash hinged at the side, the opening part of many windows.

clue.text: A glib, insane, unorthodox member of a sect

indicators.note: unorthodox means not in the standard form, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A slick, crazed heretic belongs to some fringe religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: The Albigensians were a heretical Cathar sect of medieval southern France, so unorthodox also suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Albigensians were followers of the Cathar heresy centred on Albi, so one of them belongs to that sect.

clue.text: What's said to secure good fortune

indicators.note: what is said is what is heard spoken, so a word with the same sound is wanted

explanation.surface: A charm or formula recited in the hope of locking in luck.
explanation.walkthrough: Seel is an archaic word for happiness or luck, surviving in seely.
explanation.definitionFit: Seel is an old dialect noun meaning happiness, prosperity or luck.

clue.text: Basque language unusual in UK areas

indicators.note: unusual means not in the normal form, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Hearing the Basque tongue is a rarity in British regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Euskara is the native name speakers use for their own Basque tongue.

clue.text: English maiden getting married, a nineteenth-century story

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
M for maiden, a cricket scoring abbreviation for an over with no runs
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: An English girl's wedding is the plot of an old novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane Austen's Emma (1815) ends with its heroine marrying, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is Jane Austen's novel of 1815, a story from that century.

clue.text: Insistence on observance of law upsetting 15

indicators.note: upsetting throws things out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to clue 15, a tree

explanation.surface: Strict legalism unsettles the answer to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to the answer at 15, whose letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomism is religious legalism, conduct governed by strict adherence to a moral law.

clue.text: The wanderer — he carried out legal procedure once

indicators.note: carried out means taken away, so those letters leave the first word

explanation.surface: A traveller is described as having conducted a court case in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Take HE out of THE to leave T, then add ROVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Trover was a common-law action to recover goods wrongfully taken, now historical, hence once.

clue.text: Phone order sent the wrong way leading to anger

indicators.note: going the wrong way means going backwards, so read the letters in reverse

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A phone order misdirected ends in a customer's fury.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour; reversed it starts the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobile is the everyday British word for a cell phone.

clue.text: Very good poems nevertheless included useless "flowery" bits

indicators.note: included means held within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: PI is short for pious, very good

explanation.surface: Fine verses still had some pointless floral ornament in them.
explanation.walkthrough: PI and ODES wrap round STILL: PI-STILL-ODES. PI for pious is a crossword standard.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistillode is a sterile, vestigial pistil, a non-functioning part of a flower.

clue.text: Memory coming back to old member of tribe

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: O is an abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Remembrance returns to an ancient tribesman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moro are Muslim peoples of the southern Philippines, so a Moro is one of that group.

clue.text: Perverted hope to live as a goddess

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of its proper form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A twisted ambition to exist as a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoebe is a Titaness of Greek myth and a name of Artemis as moon deity.

clue.text: Simple fellow having mark inscribed in tree

indicators.note: something inscribed is written into a surface, so it is put inside

parts.note: Simple Simon of the nursery rhyme
M for mark, a German currency

explanation.surface: A simpleton carves his initials into a tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes inside SIMON: SIM-M-ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Simmon is a short dialect form of persimmon, the fruit-bearing tree.

clue.text: Dawn's taking a very long time to pen article

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so one item is placed within the other

explanation.surface: Dawn, a writer, takes ages to write a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawn looks like a woman's name, but it is the daybreak. A sits inside EON.
explanation.definitionFit: Eoan is an adjective meaning relating to the dawn, from Eos the dawn goddess.

clue.text: The crafty drunk inclined to quarrel

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sly drinker gets argumentative.
explanation.definitionFit: Fratchety is a dialect adjective for irritable and quarrelsome, from fratch, to squabble.

clue.text: Stop loveless marriage somehow — I want a realistic approach

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are reordered
love is zero in tennis, so loveless means removing a zero-shaped letter

explanation.surface: Someone calling time on a passionless marriage says they want to be practical.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the O from STOP, then rearrange STP with MARRIAGE. The definition is in the speaker's own voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A pragmatiser is someone who makes things practical, exactly the person demanding a realistic approach.

clue.text: Colourful stuff gives Spooner's American friend trouble

indicators.note: Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of two words trade places

parts.note: bud is American slang for a pal

explanation.surface: A colourful product causes problems for a buddy across the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: Bud care, with initial sounds swapped, becomes cud bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Cudbear is a purple dye made from lichens, a colouring substance.

clue.text: Measure of brightness seen in aged plant

indicators.note: seen in means found inside, so the unit sits within the other piece

parts.note: AE abbreviates Latin aetatis, aged, as on memorials
the stilb is a unit of luminance

explanation.surface: An old plant is noted for how bright it looks.
explanation.walkthrough: The stilb is an obscure unit of luminance, one candela per square centimetre; the aged abbreviation comes from Latin on gravestones.
explanation.definitionFit: Astilbe is a garden perennial with feathery plumes of flowers.

clue.text: Hesitation by artist to make pilgrimage

explanation.surface: An artist's doubt about setting out on a sacred journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Umra is the lesser Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca, which can be made at any time of year.

clue.text: Drug cut into small pieces

explanation.surface: A narcotic is divided up for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both slang for cannabis resin and a verb meaning chop up finely.

clue.text: A team completely upset in a sort of depression

parts.note: XI, eleven, is a cricket or football side

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

explanation.surface: A side thoroughly beaten sinks into gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Depression suggests low spirits, but it is a hollow in the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The axilla is the armpit, a hollow under the arm and so a kind of depression in anatomy.

clue.text: Old ball with harps playing around entrance initially

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other
playing suggests moving about, so the letters are rearranged
initially points to the very first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A dance of old where harps are strummed as guests come in.
explanation.walkthrough: Ball seems to mean a dance, but it is a sphere. HARPS rearranged goes round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Sphaer is an archaic spelling of sphere, a globe or ball.

clue.text: Isn't ale newly brewed outstanding?

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients into something new, so the letters are recombined

explanation.surface: A beer drinker asks whether the fresh ale is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: Outstanding here means projecting or conspicuous, not excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient means prominent, standing out from its surroundings.

clue.text: French star to work with energy first and last

indicators.note: first and last means at both ends, so one piece flanks the other

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy, used at each end

explanation.surface: A French celebrity must put energy into the job from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: E appears at both ends of TOIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Étoile is the French word for star, also used for a leading ballet dancer.

clue.text: Remonstrate as old lover having claim

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to postulate is to assert or claim

explanation.surface: An ex-partner protests while asserting a right to something.
explanation.definitionFit: To expostulate is to argue earnestly in protest, which is to remonstrate.

clue.text: One knowing about law denying outsiders US protection

indicators.note: refusing the outsiders means removing the letters at both ends

parts.note: a legist is an expert in law

explanation.surface: A lawyer refuses foreigners American protection.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the first and last letters of LEGIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Egis is the American spelling of aegis, sponsorship or shielding.

clue.text: King has foreign friend, a lord

parts.note: K is king in chess notation

explanation.surface: A monarch counts a peer from abroad as a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Kami is a Japanese title of honour for a lord, as well as the word for a divine being.

clue.text: Uncivilised person irritated husband

parts.note: got, as in it really got me, means annoyed
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A boor annoyed his spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A goth is a barbarian, after the Germanic people who sacked Rome.

clue.text: Trust cut price will go up

indicators.note: going up in a down clue means reading from bottom to top
cut means docked, so the final letter goes

explanation.surface: Believe it, prices slashed now will rise.
explanation.walkthrough: WORTH loses its last letter, then reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Trow is an archaic verb meaning to believe or have faith.

clue.text: Girl appearing at end of drama inadequate, "not authentic"

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the word loses its final letter
appearing at the end means placed after, fixing the order of the parts

explanation.surface: A girl turns up at the end of a poor play which critics call fake.
explanation.walkthrough: In music, the plagal modes are contrasted with the authentic modes, so not authentic is a fair definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plagal describes a church mode or cadence opposite to the authentic kind in music theory.

clue.text: A terrible maiden being held in respect

indicators.note: being held means gripped inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: M for maiden, a cricket scoring abbreviation

explanation.surface: An awful young woman is nonetheless highly regarded.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes inside DIRE, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to esteem them, a synonym of respect as a verb.

clue.text: Vile ground, a swamp

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Nasty terrain, a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: Ground looks like land, which fits a swamp, but it signals the letters are broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: Vlei is a South African word for low marshy ground that floods seasonally.

clue.text: Wine? This writer gets to deteriorate when consuming litres

parts.note: this writer is the setter, me

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: L is the symbol for litres

explanation.surface: The setter goes downhill drinking wine by the litre.
explanation.walkthrough: This writer is the setter's usual way of saying 'me'. The question mark signals a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Merlot is a red grape variety and the wine made from it, one example of wine.

clue.text: What one expects to observe is head of monastery showing faith

parts.note: par is the normal or expected standard

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The abbot is seen practising the faith, as expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Parseeism is the Zoroastrian religion of the Parsees of India.
